content: The Texas Tech University Health Sciences Center El Paso Campus is a branch of the Texas Tech University Health Sciences Center (TTUHSC) located in El Paso, Texas. It was originally established in 1973 in partnership with Thomason Hospital as part of the TTUHSC system. Currently, the facility employs approximately 1,200 faculty and staff members. Thirdand fourth-year medical students receive their clinical training at the El Paso campus, alongside residents who are enrolled in eight accredited residency programs. The campus also operates eleven community clinics distributed throughout the city and county of El Paso. In addition to its partnership with Thomason Hospital, the El Paso campus collaborates with the William Beaumont Army Medical Center, located at Fort Bliss, and Providence Hospital. The facility is in the process of constructing three new buildings and has completed another building in preparation for the anticipated opening of a full four-year medical school in 2009. By 2013, the economic impact of TTUHSC at El Paso is projected to reach $31 billion. The institution is also poised to address critical health issues affecting border and Hispanic populations by spearheading research that will significantly contribute to the national understanding of diseases prevalent in the El Paso area, such as diabetes, obesity, and depression. In 2005, TTUHSC at El Paso initiated the Infinity Campaign, aiming to raise $25 million in private funding to support the construction of the four-year medical school. On August 4, 2007, Paul Foster, the President and CEO of Western Refining, made a historic $50 million donation to the school. This contribution represents the largest single donation in the history of the Texas Tech University System.
